chunks.arabic_text: إِمَالِي الصَّدُوقِ: عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ، عَنِ الْحِمْيَرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنِ عَنْبَسَةَ الْعَابِدِ، عَنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: From Amali al-Saduq: From Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Anbasa al-A'bid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْخِصْمَةَ فِي الدِّينِ فَإِنَّهَا تَشْغَلُ الْقَلْبَ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَتُوْرَثُ النِّفَاقَ وَتَكْسِبُ الضَّغَائِنَ وَتَسْتَجِيرُ الْكَذِبَ

translations.en: Beware of argumentation in the religion, for it diverts the heart from the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, leads to hypocrisy, brings about rancour, and justifies borrowing lies.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against excessive debate and argumentation in religious matters, noting that it distracts the heart from the remembrance of God. This practice fosters hypocrisy, generates enmity among people, and encourages the use of falsehood to win disputes.
en.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social consequences of religious argumentation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
